headline: Phillies hold off Marlins rally for fourth straight win
recap: The Phillies beat the Marlins 6-5 at Citizens Bank Park on Monday to win their fourth straight game. Philadelphia built a 4-1 lead through six innings behind Cristopher Sanchez, who allowed one run over six innings with six strikeouts to improve to 16-4. Miami then chipped away, scoring twice in the seventh off Jonathan Bowlan and once in the eighth on a Brian Navarreto homer off Brooks Raley, while the Phillies answered with a run in each of those innings to stay two runs ahead. The Marlins got one more off closer Jhoan Duran in the ninth before he closed it out for his 27th save. Bryce Harper went 3-for-4 with a walk, and Alec Bohm, Bryson Stott, Trea Turner and Kyle Schwarber each drove in a run; pinch-hitter Derek Hill added a two-run single off the bench.
Philadelphia is 68-58, second in the NL East, 6.5 games behind the first-place Braves, and has won four straight.

The Phillies continue their series with the Marlins Tuesday at Citizens Bank Park, with Zack Wheeler set to start opposite Miami's Cade Gibson. First pitch is 6:40 PM ET. DraftKings lists the Phillies as -227 favorites on the moneyline.
